review.method: Bounded read-only mechanism review; each scene checked for why/how/default/failure.

rating_legend.red: A next question would expose a materially wrong or missing state/ownership/default boundary.
rating_legend.yellow: The mechanism is usable at current granularity, but one condition or failure path should be made visible.
rating_legend.green: The four questions are answerable within current scope; retain stated version and evidence limits.

priority_gaps.gap: Make persisted state, aggregation, permission priority, lock/replay ordering, durable-vs-process background work, accepted/applied Turn state, Artifact publication, and recovery prerequisites visible.
Add event application semantics, capability-specific controls, credential/Namespace boundaries, unresolved Java persistence default, and direct-call/session/recovery limits.
Expose version/status and enterprise responsibility boundaries so broad architecture claims do not become production or SLA claims.

four_questions.why: Cross-request/process continuation needs one serialized unit for context, current reply, permission, tools, tasks and middleware state.
four_questions.how: AgentState stores session_id, summary, context, reply_context, permission_context, tool_context, tasks_context and middle_context; parked state is derived from the tail assistant message and matching tool call/result ids.
four_questions.default: State is JSON serializable; structured schema becomes JSON Schema after reload; first persistence is upsert and later update assumes an existing session.
four_questions.failure: A resolved SUBMITTED call, another Agent's observed message, stale live snapshot or post-restart schema validator must not be treated as the same parked/resumable state.

focus_evidence.state_example: S-17/R-4 with tail ToolCall C-9=ASKING, permission mode DEFAULT, activated groups basic/files -> AWAITING_PERMISSION; resume must carry R-4/C-9.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Tail C-9=SUBMITTED already has ToolResultBlock(C-9, success) -> not waiting; replaying confirmation would duplicate continuation.

four_questions.why: Model schema, streaming progress and durable context need separate objects and stable call/result identity.
four_questions.how: ToolChunk streams blocks; ToolResponse.append_chunk merges same-id text, re-encodes base64 data, updates metadata and retains severe failure state; Agent emits a ToolResultBlock with the ToolCallBlock id.
four_questions.default: Chunk starts as running; final states are success/error/interrupted/denied; URL DataBlock is not appendable; a result id must match its launching call.
four_questions.failure: Inactive/malformed calls fail before side effects; URL/different-source data append raises; later success cannot erase a previously recorded error.

focus_evidence.state_example: C-9 -> b1 text chunks "uploading " + "report.pdf" -> one result block b1; state success.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Same b1 first URL DataBlock then another URL DataBlock, or ERROR then SUCCESS; do not concatenate URLs or downgrade final error.

four_questions.why: A valid tool schema does not authorize a side effect; the decision order determines the product safety boundary.
four_questions.how: DEFAULT evaluates deny, ask, read-only, tool check, allow, fallback ASK; EXPLORE skips tool check/allow for non-read-only; BYPASS skips safety ASK; DONT_ASK converts ASK to DENY; ASK parks and emits RequireUserConfirmEvent.
four_questions.default: Read-only is per invocation; safety ASK can be immune to allow rules except in BYPASS; suggested rules can persist future matching approvals.
four_questions.failure: Unknown tool, inactive group, JSON/schema failure and mismatched resume ids do not execute; parked reply has finished_reason=null; partial confirmations do not replay unresolved asks.

focus_evidence.state_example: Write(/workspace/a.md): DEFAULT -> ASK; EXPLORE -> DENY; DONT_ASK -> DENY; same call with explicit BYPASS trust boundary may pass tool checks.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Allow rule cannot override EXPLORE write denial or a DEFAULT safety ASK; BYPASS is not a sandbox.

four_questions.why: A browser connection must not own a long tool's lifetime, and completion must wake the original session without a second submission.
four_questions.how: ToolOffloadMiddleware yields a placeholder; BackgroundTaskManager holds a process-local asyncio watcher and bus registry; completion pushes session inbox plus wakeup; WakeupDispatcher reruns under session lock; ToolStop cancels same-session local work or broadcasts remote cancellation.
four_questions.default: The watcher is process-local and TTL-registered, not a durable execution engine; browser disconnect is observation loss only; bus/storage are the durable handoff pieces.
four_questions.failure: Process restart loses the watcher; unknown/cross-session task ids fail; parked sessions must not be forced into a None run; late results need original task/session identity and state reconciliation.

focus_evidence.state_example: C-9 -> B-7 submitted; browser disconnect; B-7 completes on W2 -> inbox(S-17)+wakeup -> lock -> next reasoning.
focus_evidence.counterexample: After disconnect, POSTing the original Msg again creates a second B-8; a registry record alone does not prove a watcher survived process exit.

four_questions.why: Lock prevents concurrent state ownership; replay lets a late or reconnecting observer catch up. Neither replaces the other.
four_questions.how: Python bus uses tokenized NX/EX lock with heartbeat, append-only bounded replay plus transient pub/sub; ChatService takes the run lock before loading state and persists reply/state/cursor before releasing it. Java uses resource-specific snapshot/as_of/cursor projection and fresh snapshot after 410.
four_questions.default: Python session replay cap is 1000 entries; live pub/sub is fire-and-forget; Java native seq, Service SSE cursor, idempotency key and request id are distinct identities.
four_questions.failure: Expired/crashed lock can be taken over, but stale holder cannot delete a new token; stale snapshots must not overwrite live state; expired cursor requires snapshot, not task resubmission.

focus_evidence.state_example: Subscribe first, replay after cursor, dedup the seam by entry id; persist checkpoint/state under the short checkpoint lock while the run lock is still held.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Subscribe only to pub/sub after a disconnect or read state before acquiring the run lock; both lose events or permit stale overwrite.

four_questions.why: Business callers need stable logical work identity across retries, queues, approvals and page reconnects.
four_questions.how: Session freezes target/config; Turn is one logical request; run is one execution attempt; idempotency key + identical body retrieves the same Turn; accepted input can wait before applied consumption; capabilities gate steer/inject/actions/resume.
four_questions.default: 202 queued is accepted-not-complete; later Turns queue behind an approval; Managed retains context, Team/Workflow Turns start independent work; observer reads do not execute.
four_questions.failure: New key duplicates work; changed body conflicts; completed/cancelled Turn cannot resume; action/steer on closed or unsupported target is rejected; resume does not undo external effects.

focus_evidence.state_example: S1/T1/R1 accepted -> queued; T2 remains queued while T1 awaits approval; same key/body returns T1; approval makes input applied and continuation runs.
focus_evidence.counterexample: SSE disconnect followed by new key k2 resubmission creates T2; GET events is drawn as an inference call; accepted receipt is drawn as applied/completed.

four_questions.why: Execution workspace visibility and business deliverability are different contracts.
four_questions.how: Capability check -> session-bound file_id input -> workspace work -> explicit Artifact publication -> metadata/access verification -> download; Team/Workflow members exchange accessible artifacts rather than an implicit shared filesystem.
four_questions.default: Managed upload limit is 16 MiB; file_input differs by target; working-directory files and Host files are not automatically application-downloadable; completed is not verified delivery.
four_questions.failure: Cross-session file references, guessed paths, unsupported file_input and inaccessible artifacts fail; external URI publication does not copy or grant access; wrong content/version still needs business rejection.

focus_evidence.state_example: F-1 uploaded to S1 -> Turn input; generated F-2 verified -> publish -> A-7 -> application reads A-7 metadata then downloads F-2.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Agent says /workspace/report.pdf exists, but no F-2/A-7 record; application treats the path as a public download or assumes Team Lead sees member disk.

four_questions.why: A durable view is useful only if state, workspace, credentials, ownership and external effects can be reconciled.
four_questions.how: Harness/Service persist different layers; checkpoint restores working state but not OS/tool/provider progress; uncertain calls require business lookup and reconcile; database, workspace/artifact snapshot and original Vault key must restore together.
four_questions.default: Java source pages disagree on the Harness default (EVENT_LOG/native checkpoints vs JsonFileAgentStateStore); distributed production requires DistributedStore/remote state and execution guards; Java Service is prerelease.
four_questions.failure: Stale writer lease, missing key, mismatched backup point, provider session gone, expired cursor or external write after checkpoint blocks safe resume; recovery is not rollback.

focus_evidence.state_example: C-9 uncertain after crash -> query order system -> reconcile verified ToolResult -> resume same Turn; restore DB+workspace+artifact+Vault key from one point.
focus_evidence.counterexample: Restore checkpoint and immediately replay create_order, or restore DB without original Vault key and call it recovered.
